outcome.technical: Why no-base: run-test-gate.base_red read the ledger only through _evidence_io.base_run, which takes a row at the head on a CLEAN tree. Every k02/k03r row was a task gate on HEAD plus the work (k02's row: 'git described the tree before the run; 5 dirty path(s)'), and nothing ever recorded a clean run at either base, so every reading was no-base. Changes: (1) _evidence_io.py - BASE_SCOPE/BASE_OF_KEY (a base run's row: subject_key gives it no subject, so no pointer is written or reconciled onto it; row_for carries baseOf); DERIVED_PHASE_GATE_ARM + derived_step_suites(); step_runs_suite(); base_run(..., suites=) also accepts a row with a step known to have run one of the suites, so a derived step spelled differently at base is found. (2) run-test-gate.py - base_red compares BY FAILING CASE per script: step_cases()/_case_key() read the row's failing lines (P157.2's `<script>: FAIL <label>` lines, keyed by script + house id, label when no id; a row-clipped label matched by its head via _same_case; another runner's line up to ' - '); _suite_at_base() says at-base only when the base lines name every case the task names in that suite; a cut list (CASES_CUT, now the one spelling failing_lines writes) or one-sided case list is not-knowable; _charge_step matches a derived step per suite via step_runs_suite, not by name. New `--base-of RUN_ID` (with --tree, no --task): reruns that row's red steps by their verbatim names and commands in the tree, records a BASE_SCOPE row (no ids, no pointer, no boundary, like a full run), prints base_reading of the task run against rows + that row (--json for the drive).
